### claim_ext_dependency_redetermination

- Hub `dependency_redetermination_credit_74e82837`: trigger sentence ("issued on … whose dependents on record exceed …"), effect (allowance, MBA and balance raised, next determination number, entitlement-credit entry), tool `record_dependency_redetermination_c7b3c182` with parameters matching the runtime schema. Equivalent.
- Baseline (`baseline.rule`) → `dependency_redetermination_credit_computation_178d6248`: per-dependent = program figure, count capped at the program maximum, rounded to the cent; increase = redetermined − on-claim, ≥ 0; credit = maximum duration weeks × increase, capped by base-period-wage fraction × BPW − MBA on the claim, rounded down, ≥ 0. Order ("weeks multiply … then compared with the wage cap … rounding applied to the lesser figure") present. Product figures named and found: facet "Dependency Allowance Rates" (15.00 / 3), facet "Entitlement Duration…" (26 weeks, 0.3333). Equivalent. Observation: the inputs table also lists "Weekly benefit amount | The claim", which the baseline rule never reads (no normative effect; see dependency_form).
- Factor `per_dependent_amount_redetermination` → `family_rate_per_dependent_on_redetermination_1b9d9574`: 2+ & ≥ 182 days → 18.00; 2+ & < 182 → 16.00; otherwise program amount; age definition (effective date → handling date). Full ladder, exact.
- Factor `credited_weeks_redetermination` → `credited_weeks_for_added_dependents_7789a548`: ≥ 13 → balance ÷ (WBA + allowance on the claim), rounded up; 1–12 → 0.75 × max weeks rounded to whole week; none → max weeks; "weekly payments" = entries of kind weekly. Full ladder, exact (divisor = allowance before the redetermination, matching compute `da_old`).
- Factor `allowance_ceiling_redetermination` → `redetermination_allowance_ceiling_3ea0f958`: > 90 days → 0.075 × WBA; 22–90 → 0.08 × WBA; ≤ 21 → none; rounded to the cent; applied before the subtraction. Full ladder, exact.
- Factor `wage_cap_fraction_redetermination` → `steady_earner_wage_cap_fraction_11fbf161`: standard + BPW ≥ 3.0 × HQW + credited ≥ floor(program fraction × BPW) → 0.36; alternate + same → 0.35; otherwise program fraction; "entitlement credited" = sum of entitlement-credit entries. All parts of the compound condition present. Exact.
- Overwrites → `policy_monetary_determination_e40722e9` clauses 3 (dependency allowance) and 4 (maximum benefit amount) written "Retired clause, no longer in force". Present, marked retired.

## kb_to_source

- Every normative sentence in the hubs, computation documents and factor documents above traces to the extended rule, its compute, the base rule or the tool contract. Interpretive additions checked and found entailed by the compute: "A fraud overpayment counts whatever its status" (compute counts all fraud rows); "Supplemental payments and reissues are not weekly payments" (filter `payment_kind='weekly'`); "The dependency allowance in the divisor is the allowance on the claim before the redetermination" (`da_old`); "Does the function decide the allowance or the credit? No" (tool body); "The function serves claims of programs not charged to employers" (tool docstring).
- Cross-problem operational guidance ("if unmet, first call …"): none found in any document.
- Opening world state written as policy fact: none (no hypothetical uses this task's figures 450.00 / 11700.00 / 36093.61 / 150.00 / 252.00 / 274.00 or its dates).
- Additions without source: none of normative force. Non-normative inaccuracy: `dependency_redetermination_credit_computation_178d6248` inputs table lists "Weekly benefit amount | The claim", an input the baseline rule does not read (true of the policy as a whole through its ceiling factor).
- Policy-side notes (source residues the KB faithfully carries; not KB verdicts):
  1. `facet_entitlement_and_benefit_year_bcf68dee` describes the EB 0.5 as "the fraction of a parent regular claim's maximum benefit amount that caps Extended Benefits entitlement" — that is `parameter_schema.eb_regular_mba_fraction`'s description, whose only consuming clause is retired by `claim_ext_extension_entitlement`. A reader who trusted the facet alone could apply a 0.5 × parent-MBA cap (here 0.5 × 12048.00 = 6024.00) the governing EB document no longer contains; the retired clause in `policy_extended_trade_disaster_entitlement` and the EB amount document settle it. Undeclared residue of an overridden clause in the parameter schema.
  2. Same facet's hypothetical says "whether that cap or the duration figure governs is decided by the monetary determination rules" — the clause that decided it (base MBA lesser-of) is retired; the pointer now lands on a retired clause.
  3. `facet_special_program_qualifying_terms_390c0cf9` lists "Extended Benefits (EB): 20 weeks of full-time employment in the base period" (`eb_min_weeks_employment`), while the replaced_by clause proves the minimum weeks "through their wage equivalent" at 40 × WBA. Consistent with the replaced_by wording, but the source never states how 20 weeks maps to 40 × WBA.
  4. `claim_ext_extension_entitlement.cross_category[overpay].note` speaks of "its classification penalty share", which neither the rule nor the compute uses.
- Rule/compute disagreements in this task's policies: none that move a value. Minor: `claim_ext_payment_election_lead` compute `other_verified` takes the latest case of any pathway (ITVR included) where the rule says "of any other pathway" — equivalent in every reachable case (an ITVR outside 30 days that is the latest implies no other case within 30 days). `credited_weeks` "rounded to the whole week" is `RND(…, 0)`; no program's maximum weeks × 0.75 lands on an ambiguous half other than 19.5 (→ 20 under both half-up and half-even).

### source_to_kb (round 2)

- All four prerequisite sentences of this task's tree: verbatim, state form, only in their blocked hubs (mechanical check over 79 docs: supplemental ×2 → `supplemental_shortfall_payment_380923a8`; EB ×2 → `extended_benefits_first_determination_20f6f272`).
- Baselines and every factor ladder of `claim_ext_dependency_redetermination`, `claim_ext_payment_election_lead`, `claim_ext_parent_shortfall_supplement`, `claim_ext_extension_entitlement` re-compared against the round-5 rule, ladders and compute: all tiers, thresholds, shares, rounding and order exact (changed ones listed in the closure table; the rest unchanged from round 1 and still exact).
- Overwrites: same ten retired clauses, each still marked retired in its bearing document; no undeclared retirement.
- Variant parameters (all programs) still match the facets value for value.
- **Finding (KB-BIJECTION):** `facet_entitlement_and_benefit_year_bcf68dee` was reworded by the renderer. Round 1 carried the source's parameter meaning ("the fraction of a parent regular claim's maximum benefit amount that caps Extended Benefits entitlement"; column "Extended Benefits fraction of the parent's maximum benefit amount"). Round 2 carries "the scheduled Extended Benefits fraction", column "Extended Benefits fraction", note "An Extended Benefits fraction of 0 means the claim is not an Extended Benefits claim; the figure is 0.5 for the Extended Benefits (EB) program". The source parameter text it must carry is unchanged: `eb_regular_mba_fraction: "Fraction of the parent regular claim's maximum benefit amount that caps Extended Benefits entitlement (decimal); 0 means not an Extended Benefits claim"`. The "0 means …" half is carried; the "fraction of the parent regular claim's maximum benefit amount that caps Extended Benefits entitlement" half has no home anywhere in the corpus (grep for "parent's maximum benefit amount", "parent regular claim's maximum", "caps Extended": no hit outside the retired clause in `policy_extended_trade_disaster_entitlement_2031d6de`). Nature: the source still carries a parameter meaning that contradicts the in-force EB rule (an undeclared residue of the overridden base clause — round-1 policy-side note 1); the rendering removes the contradiction by dropping the source's side of it rather than the source resolving it. The documents are now internally consistent, but they no longer translate a source atom. No scored value moves (the EB amount document governs; 7089 unaffected).
